paras: The beating of Wemer by regulators near Pilot Grove was an attack in Cooper County, Missouri, in February 1881, in which 'improvised regulators' seized a German youth accused of ravishing an eight-year-old girl and beat him nearly to death. They also lashed his father, and the only known account, in the Sedalia Weekly Bazoo, presented the beating as deserved but partial punishment.

According to the Bazoo, the accused, aged seventeen or eighteen, lived on a farm next to the girl's family about two and a half miles from Pilot Grove, and both attended Mt. Vernon school. He was accused of dragging her from the road in thick woods and assaulting her as they walked home from school late in the week before 15 February.

Her father found signs of a struggle at the spot and 'determined upon vengeance,' and as word spread 'the excitement ran high.' The next day a body of 'improvised regulators' called at the residence of Wemer senior, took the youth into custody, and 'thrashed until life was well nigh extinct.' The father, whom the Bazoo described as having been 'in the clutches of the law,' tried to excuse his son and received 'a number of lashes over his back, until he begged for mercy.'
No report of a legal arrest, a trial, action against the regulators, or the youth's recovery appears in the coverage.

The Bazoo printed the story on 15 February 1881 under the headline 'A YOUTHFUL RAVISHER,' from what an unnamed Pilot Grove gentleman told its reporter. It withheld the girl's name, treated the accusation as established, and said in a subhead that 'the Brute is Partially Punished for His Crime.' The paper wrote that his age alone saved him 'from a deserved death' and that 'the only wonder' was that the case did not end in 'a hanging bee.'
No other report was found, and the account names no race for anyone involved.

accounts.label: Pilot Grove informant via Sedalia Bazoo
accounts.gist: A neighbor youth assaulted the girl on the road home from school; the next day regulators took him from his father's house and beat him nearly to death, and whipped the father for trying to condone the offense.

framing.detail: Headlines 'A YOUTHFUL RAVISHER' and 'the Brute is Partially Punished for His Crime'; the paper treated the accusation as fact, called the death he escaped 'deserved,' and regretted the absence of 'a hanging bee.'

record_check.dossier: Two victims: the youth Wemer and his father, Wemer senior. The text spells the name 'Wemer' four times; 'Wiener' appears once in the raw page OCR.
Described as 'a young German'; no race stated, and nothing indicates a Black victim.
mob_assault: 'improvised regulators', an ad hoc group taking revenge for one alleged crime, not an organized band.
